features.title: From scattered agent setups to maintainable Team assets.
features.subtitle: CrewBee focuses on the maintainability of agent workflows: Team assets, workflow rules, tools / skills strategy, reviews, and completion criteria.

cards.title: Build reusable Teams for specialized workflows
cards.desc: Not just agents: define tools / skills strategy, workflow rules, shared policies, reviews, and completion criteria. Turn a repeatable way of working into a reusable Team.

cards.title: Keep simple tasks lightweight; add support when complexity requires it
cards.desc: CrewBee does not make multi-agent collaboration a default ritual. Simple tasks can stay on a fast single-agent path; complex tasks can add support agents, review, validation, and completion criteria.

cards.title: The Leader owns the decision context
cards.desc: The Leader gathers user goals, project constraints, support findings, review feedback, validation results, and risks, then makes the final judgment and handoff.

cards.title: Delegate with isolated contexts
cards.desc: Support agents work in isolated contexts for codebase exploration, research, or review. They return findings, evidence, risks, and recommendations without polluting the main context.

why.titleAfterBreak: need a reviewable, verifiable work structure.
paragraphs: Code generation is only one part. Reliable software delivery also needs requirements understanding, codebase exploration, implementation planning, focused changes, independent review, validation, and delivery notes.
When these responsibilities are scattered across prompts, agents, rules, and ad-hoc conventions, agent work becomes difficult to maintain. CrewBee turns them into reusable Agent Team assets.
why.emphasis: CrewBee’s value is not more agents by default. It is reusable Team assets for responsibilities, rules, reviews, workflows, and completion criteria.

before: Completion criteria are hard to reuse
after: Reviews and completion criteria are reusable
Simple tasks stay lightweight; complex tasks get support

how.title: How CrewBee works
how.subtitle: Define Teams as assets, connect them to OpenCode, choose a Leader or Executor, and run the workflow that matches the task.

steps.desc: Define the Team mission, Leader, members, shared policy, workflow, tools / skills strategy, review path, and completion criteria.
OpenCode is the first officially supported host. CrewBee makes Team assets selectable and runnable as agent workflows in OpenCode.
Pick Leader for complex tasks that need ownership, delegation, review, validation, and final handoff. Pick Executor for clear, local, low-risk tasks.
Simple tasks use the lightweight path; complex tasks add codebase exploration, focused implementation, independent review, validation, and delivery notes.

modes.label: Leader
modes.desc: Owns requirements understanding, task thread, support delegation, review synthesis, final judgment, and handoff notes.

modes.label: Executor
modes.desc: Best for clear, local implementation, fixes, and debugging. It does not own the complex task thread.

team.title: Team packages are engineering assets. Copy, modify, and contribute them.
paragraphs: A CrewBee Team is not a prompt file. It is a structured Team package with mission, Leader, members, shared policy, workflow, tools / skills strategy, review criteria, completion criteria, and human-readable documentation.
Start with the built-in Coding Team. Copy a template. Adjust roles, shared policy, tools / skills strategy, reviews, and completion criteria. Turn your own way of working into a reusable Team.

inspired.title: Inspired by the open-source Agent ecosystem.
paragraphs: CrewBee is inspired by community projects such as OpenCode and oh-my-openagent. These projects make the value of Agent Team workflows in real development environments clearer.
CrewBee continues in this direction by organizing Agent Teams into manageable, projectable, configurable, and reusable engineering assets.

items.a: No. CrewBee uses prompts, but its core is Team definitions, Agent profiles, delegation tooling, reviews, and completion criteria. It turns agent workflows into maintainable, runnable Team assets.

items.q: Is CrewBee a flat agent list?
items.a: No. CrewBee is not just more roles. It emphasizes Teams, Leaders, members, shared policy, workflow, reviews, and completion criteria.

No. CrewBee is designed as a Team definition layer for agent harnesses. OpenCode is the first officially supported host because it provides a practical path today. The long-term direction is to keep Team definitions portable and adapt them to more agent harnesses over time.

items.q: Does CrewBee make every task multi-agent?
items.a: No. CrewBee does not turn multi-agent work into a default ritual. Simple tasks stay lightweight; complex tasks add codebase exploration, focused implementation, independent review, validation, and handoff notes.

items.q: Why does the main agent / Leader matter?
items.a: In complex work, support agents only see part of the picture. CrewBee keeps goals, constraints, support findings, review feedback, verification results, and risks together in the main agent’s decision context.

Support agents do code exploration, research, review, or multimodal reading in dedicated contexts, then return high-signal findings to the main agent. This reduces main-agent context pollution and attention load.

items.q: Where does CrewBee sit in the OpenCode ecosystem?
items.a: CrewBee uses OpenCode as the current primary host, not as its whole identity. It is a Team definition layer that organizes prompts, agents, rules, reviews, and completion criteria into maintainable Team assets that can later be adapted to more agent harnesses.

items.q: Is Project Context fully implemented today?
items.a: No. Project Context is a Roadmap / Next-stage direction. The goal is to help long-running project agents avoid onboarding from zero every session, not to claim a mature current capability.
OpenCode is the first officially supported host. More Agent Harness adapters are planned.

Yes. CrewBee’s core is Team definition and projection, so you can create ResearchOpsTeam, DocumentationTeam, MarketingOpsTeam, ReleaseOpsTeam, and more. The flagship public example today is the built-in Coding Team.
The easiest contribution is not changing the core runtime. Contribute Team templates, docs, use cases, installation feedback, FAQ improvements, or show your Team in Discussions.
